sentences.text: Gwalior, Dated : 06-07-2018 Shri Vaibhav Maheshwari, learned counsel for the appellants.
Shri G.S.Chauhan, learned Public Prosecutor for the State.

Appellants have filed this appeal under the provisions of Section 71(6) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 (for brevity "the Act of 2006") being aggrieved by judgment dated 26.8.2016 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Morena, in Criminal Appeal No.78/2016 confirming the order dated 31.10.15 passed by the Adjudicating officer cum Additional District Magistrate Distt. Morena in case No.26/14.
The prosecution case in short is that on 20.10.13 a Tanker bearing No.MP06 GA 0357 driven by appellant No.1 and owned by appellant No.2 was stopped.
Food Safety Officer Ms. Rekha Soni introduced herself and asked for the documents pertaining to the Tanker.
In presence of the driver and owner of the goods Pramod Sharma, sample of milk was taken after completing formalities of giving intimation under form 5A.
Sample was sent for testing and report of the Public Analyst was obtained.
According to which, milk fat was 0.2%, whereas the minimum limit is 4.5%.

Similarly,
solids not fat were found to be 7.18% and minimum prescribed standard is 8.5%.
Test for formalin was also found to be positive.
As per the report, the sample was found to be sub- standard under Section 3 (2x).

In view of such report, prosecution was lodged and the Additional District Magistrate and Adjudicating officer, Morena, passed order dated 31.10.15 imposing a penalty of Rs. five lac on appellant No.1 Arun Tiwari and similarly penalty of Rs. five lac on appellant No.2- Pramod Sharma.

entities.text: Additional District Magistrate and Adjudicating officer,
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This order was challenged before the learned Sessions Judge/Tribunal which has affirmed the order of the Adjudicating officer.

On behalf of the appellants, it is submitted that appellant No.1 is only a driver, and therefore, there was no justification in imposing penalty on him inasmuch as he was not responsible for such penalty in terms of the provisions contained in Section 51 of the Act of 2006.
It is also submitted that there is no evidence on record to show that owner of the goods is appellant No.2 and this burden was to be discharged by the prosecution.

He also submits that no independent witness before whom sample was taken was examined before the Adjudicating officer and in 2 CRA-1268-2016 absence of such examination, the orders passed by the Adjudicating officer and the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal,
Morena, are liable to be set aside.
Learned counsel for the appellants, however, admitted that he has not disputed taking of the sample from the custody of the appellants.
It is also admitted that no appeal was filed in terms of the provisions contained in Section 46(4) of the Act of 2006 against the report of Food Analyst before the Designated Officer.
In view of such facts, non- compliance of the provisions of the Act and sample being sub-standard as defined in Section 3(2x) stands proved.

sentences.text: Sub-Section 4 of Section 46 of the Act of 2006 provides that an appeal against the report of Food Analyst shall lie before the Designated Officer who shall, if he so decides, refer the matter to the referral food laboratory as notified by the Food Authority for opinion.
In the present case, sampling process is not under challenge.
As has been admitted by the learned counsel for the appellants, no appeal was filed to challenge the report of Food Analyst.
Thus, that report showing sample taken to be sub-standard is also conclusive.

Thus, the only issue as to whether both the driver and the owner will be liable to pay the penalty separately in terms of the provisions contained in Section 3(2x) of the Act because as per the definition contained in Section 3(1)(n) "food business" includes manufacture, processing, packaging, storage, transportation, distribution of food, import and includes food services, catering services, sale of food or food ingredients.

Since sample has been taken from the joint custody of the driver and the owner of the goods, separate liability cannot be fastened on each of them separately inasmuch as Section 51 provides penalty for manufacturing for sale, selling, storing or importing etc. of sub-standards food for human consumption and makes it liable to pay a fine which may extend to Rs. five lac.

Since driver was only driving the tanker and there is nothing on record to show that he was aware about the adulteration made in the milk and he used it for his own gain, therefore, in the opinion of this Court, no separate liability could have been fastened on the driver.
To that extent, appeal deserves to be allowed and is allowed.
Penalty imposed on appellant No.1 is set aside.
Arguments advanced by learned counsel for the appellants that onus was on the prosecution to have proved that appellant No.2 is the owner of the goods is devoid of merits.

Onus was on the appellants to have shown that from where they procured the material and their saying 3 CRA-1268-2016 that it was to be delivered at Morena barrier to some person was not sufficient because adulteration is to be seen at the point of taking of sample and till that point the third person to whom the goods were to be supplied had not come into picture, therefore, the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the appellants that appellant No.2 is also not liable to pay the penalty deserves to be rejected and is hereby rejected.
The order passed in relation to appellant No.2, owner of the goods, is maintained.
With the aforesaid directions, the appeal is disposed of.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE ms/-
